title: VR-Pipe: Streamlining Hardware Graphics Pipeline for Volume Rendering
problem: Radiance field rendering methods (e.g., 3D Gaussian Splatting) are evaluated only on software-based shader pipelines, leaving performance on fixed-function GPU hardware graphics units unexplored and suboptimal for volume rendering workloads.
motivation: Radiance field and neural rendering methods produce high-quality photorealistic images but require real-time frame rates; existing fixed-function GPU graphics pipelines were not designed for the alpha-compositing, early-termination, and tile-binning characteristics of volume rendering.
method: VR-Pipe adds two optimizations to GPU hardware for volume rendering. First, it repurposes the depth-test units (specialized hardware that normally checks which objects are in front) to stop ray marching once pixels become fully opaque, avoiding wasted computation. Second, it pre-blends fragments (pixel colors) in the programmable shader cores by grouping them into tiles and merging quads before passing them to the fixed-function blending hardware, which removes the blending bottleneck. The design targets 3D Gaussian Splatting.
key_novelty: VR-Pipe makes volume rendering efficient on fixed-function GPU hardware by repurposing depth-test units for early termination and using multi-granular tile binning with quad merging to pre-blend fragments in shader cores before fixed-function blending.
contributions: First systematic performance analysis of radiance field rendering (3DGS) on the hardware GPU graphics pipeline using graphics APIs
Native hardware early termination mechanism for volume rendering by repurposing existing fixed-function GPU units
Multi-granular tile binning with quad merging to reduce fixed-function blending bottlenecks
Up to 2.78x speedup over the conventional graphics pipeline with negligible hardware overhead

metrics.speedup: up to 2.78x over conventional GPU graphics pipeline

limitations: Evaluation is specific to 3D Gaussian Splatting; generalization to other radiance field or neural rendering methods is not fully quantified.
primary_theme: hardware graphics pipeline optimization for volume/radiance-field rendering
